report:
The claim is accurate and well-supported.

**FDA approval and labeling:** Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, 19.5 mg) received FDA approval in September 2016 specifically "for Prevention of Pregnancy for up to Five Years" (https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/fda-approves-bayers-kyleena-gavin-cooper). The official FDA prescribing label states directly: "Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years. Replace the system after 5 years if continued use is desired" (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/208224s000lbl.pdf).

**Clinical trial evidence:** This approval was based on a Phase III trial involving 1,452 healthy women aged 18–35. The device demonstrated a Pearl Index of 0.29 over five years, indicating over 99% effectiveness annually in preventing pregnancy, with generally good tolerability (https://www.drugs.com/history/kyleena.html). Additional prescribing data show a cumulative 5-year pregnancy rate of approximately 1.45% (based on 13 pregnancies, Kaplan-Meier estimate), reinforcing high long-term efficacy across the full five-year period.

**Corroboration:** Multiple independent secondary sources—including patient education sites and manufacturer resources—consistently confirm the five-year duration and describe Kyleena's efficacy as comparable to sterilization, consistent with other long-acting reversible contraceptives (https://www.verywellhealth.com/kyleena-iud-4119899).

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly supports the claim. Kyleena is FDA-approved based on robust Phase III clinical trial data specifically for pregnancy prevention over a five-year period, with the official prescribing label explicitly confirming this indication and instructing replacement after five years if continued contraception is desired.
